transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Lena Morris (Redwood AE), Carlos Vega (Redwood SE), Ava Patel (Peregrine Lead ML Eng), Marcus Lin (Peregrine Infra Eng), Nina Cho (Peregrine PM)

Summary: quick hands-on SDK walkthrough, auth patterns, environment setup and sandbox run, alignment on POC and security questions.

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros?
[00:05] Ava: Ava here, lead ML, mainly build inference pipelines for clinical summarization, hi.
[00:09] Marcus: Marcus infra, I'll own network and security bits.
[00:12] Nina: Nina product, timeline and success metrics.
[00:15] Carlos: Carlos, infra/SE at Redwood, I'll run the demo and the benchmark runbook.
[00:18] Lena: Great. Objective today is a hands-on SDK sprint: python + typescript quickstarts, auth options, environment setup and a sample run in your sandbox. We'll cover caveats around PHI and private deployment too.

[02:12] Carlos: Alright I'm going to share my screen — starting with repo layout. We keep two tiny samples: quickstart_py and quickstart_ts. The py one uses our redwood SDK pip package, ts one is from npm.
[03:01] Carlos: Example env vars: REDWOOD_API_KEY or for service accounts REDWOOD_SA_KEY, plus REDWOOD_ORG if you have multiple. For local dev we recommend dotenv for secrets, for CI use secret manager.
[03:27] Marcus: Quick Q — are API keys long lived? We want rotation policies.
[03:30] Lena: API keys can be short lived if you mint them via our control plane; we also support OIDC/SSO and service account keys with rotation. Carlos will show the workflow.

[05:05] Carlos: Showing python sample: pip install redwood-inference (note: pkg name may be slightly different in registry, transcriber: package name spelled as "redwood inference" here), then set REDWOOD_API_KEY. Code snippet — client = Redwood(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) then client.generate(...).
[06:18] Carlos: Running the sample now — hitting hosted endpoint in us-west1, streaming output. (audio: keyboard clicks) 
[06:45] Speaker 1: mm-hmm
[07:01] Ava: The streaming looks good. What's the default model?
[07:05] Carlos: Default is a curated open model alias we call rdx-small in hosted, but you can pin specific model versions like rdx-2.1-fp16 or a quantized variant. We recommend starting with mid-sized for latency tests.

[09:00] Carlos: For TS example: npm install @redwood/inference, then set env REWOOD_API_KEY — actually typo in example, should be REDWOOD_API_KEY, noted. Then new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }). Generate call similar.
[10:20] Nina: Any CI pattern for key rotation?
[10:25] Carlos: We recommend using short-lived service account tokens minted via our control plane + your identity provider; otherwise use vault + periodic rotate. We have a sample GitHub action in the repo.

[12:40] Marcus: On networking: will we need VPC peering for private deployment or for dedicated? If we do hosted can we restrict by IP?
[12:48] Lena: Hosted supports IP allowlist for egress and inbound webhook callbacks; Dedicated and Private support VPC peering and private connectivity. For PHI workloads, many customers choose Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) with KMS integration.
[13:30] Marcus: KMS — can we use our AWS KMS?
[13:35] Carlos: Yes, KMS/HSM integration supported. For Private we can integrate with your KMS; for Hosted we can bring your CMKs in some enterprise packages. We'll send the exact notes in the security pack.

[15:05] Carlos: Back to code, showing how to stream and handle tokens. We show the continuous batching example: set batch_size in client config or use the platform auto-batching. Remember batching trades latency for throughput.
[16:10] Ava: Our SLO is 300ms median for 512 tokens — does that seem attainable?
[16:17] Carlos: For hosted with a mid-sized model and low sequence length yes, but depends on concurrency. You may prefer Dedicated to get predictable p95s. We'll propose a baseline during the POC.

[18:55] Carlos: Now demoing prefix caching and KV cache usage — caching helps for chat history reuse. Note: demo artifacts contained some transcriber typos e.g., KV cache referred to as KV cash earlier.
[20:00] Lena: Security checklist — SOC 2 present, we also have ISO readiness for some customers. For audit logs, Console surfaces token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and we retain logs per contract.
[20:45] Nina: For compliance, we need data residency in eu-west. Is that available?
[20:50] Carlos: Yes EU regions supported in our hosted plane; for strict residency customers often choose Private.

[23:10] Alex? (unlabeled):
[23:22] Marcus: (interrupt) do you have a sample perf test we can run locally?
[23:28] Carlos: Yes, benchmark runbook in repo. It's a python script that fires variable concurrency and reports latency percentiles to stdout and CSV. We'll run a small one now against the sandbox. 
[25:05] (sound of commands)
[25:30] Carlos: Results coming in — warm tokens, cold start penalties small. Remember quantization reduces memory and can improve throughput but may affect quality. We'll attach quantization profiles and recommended model variants.

[28:12] Ava: On quality — we need to ensure summarization accuracy isn't degraded. How do you guard against regressions during rollouts?
[28:20] Lena: We have Redwood Optimize: eval sets tied to changelogs, automatic regression alerts when quality drops. You can pin models and run canary traffic. Carlos: we'll show a brief screenshot in the pack.

[30:40] Carlos: Quick note on cost: per-token pricing for hosted, plus reserved capacity tiers for Dedicated. We can run cost estimates with your throughput numbers. There is also intelligent batching/caching that lowers per-token costs.
[31:10] Nina: Who typically owns the Dedicated purchase — infra or procurement?
[31:14] Lena: Usually procurement signs the reserved capacity; infra sponsors technical requirements. We'll coordinate with your procurement if you move forward.

[33:00] Marcus: Networking again — for Private we need to know firewall rules and egress constraints, we'll share a diagram.
[33:07] Lena: Yes please add that to Marcus' action item. We'll review.

[34:20] Carlos: Back to quickstarts: demo shows both py and ts samples running against sandbox and streaming. Also showed postman/curl examples. Note: cURL sample uses Authorization: Bearer <REDWOOD_API_KEY>.
[36:45] Ava: Can we embed Redwood SDK in our microservices? Any notable language limitations?
[36:52] Carlos: No, SDKs are lightweight; just ensure you manage keys via environment or service accounts. For high throughput we suggest using the HTTP2 streaming path or gRPC if you're on Private.

[39:00] Lena: Ok let's surface open questions from your side.
[39:06] Nina: Timeline — we want a 6 week POC, success is meeting median latency <350ms and cost per call under $0.08 for our summarization workload.
[39:17] Lena: Noted. We'll shape the POC to that.
[39:25] Marcus: Security: need SOC2 report, encryption at rest, and KMS notes. Also legal will want data deletion SLA.
[39:35] Lena: We'll share the security pack and legal checklist.

[41:00] Carlos: One thing to watch: if you enable aggressive prefix caching and re-use, throughput is great but you have to be careful about state size. We'll add recommended TTLs.

[43:12] (brief silence, typing)
[43:25] Lena: Recap: Redwood will provision a sandbox, send quickstart links, share security docs and benchmark runbook. Peregrine will share prompt set and confirm networking constraints. Schedule benchmark with Carlos for week of 11/17.
[44:00] Nina: Sounds good. Any blockers?
[44:05] Marcus: Only confirming VPC peering options — I'll get that doc to you.
[44:10] Ava: I'll pull together a 100-example prompt set for summarization.

[46:22] Carlos: Small gotcha I saw in your repo notes — make sure your env var names match. Some early examples had REWOOD_API_KEY misspelled; we fixed it in the main branch.
[46:40] Ava: (laughs) good to know.

[48:00] Lena: Next meeting cadence — probably 1:1 POC kickoff with SE and your infra. We can also invite procurement if you want pricing early.
[48:12] Nina: Let's do SE + infra next week for a deep infra handshake.

[50:10] Lena: Alright thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and action items.
[50:18] Meeting ends.
questions: Can Redwood support AWS KMS for encryption?
What are rotation options for API keys and service accounts?
Is EU data residency supported for hosted?
notes: Transcriber imperfect: some package names and env var typos (REWOOD/REDWOOD) appear
Customer cares about PHI and latency SLOs; likely candidate for Private or Dedicated POC
